sentences.text:
Writ Petition (Ms) No. 1536 of 2024
M/s Jamini Pharmaceuticals.

..............Petitioner.
 Versus
National Highway Authority of India
and another. ............Respondents

Present:
Mr. Gaurav Singh, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Hon'ble Mr. Justice Rakesh Thapliyal
1.

By the instant writ petition, petitioner is praying for expeditious disposal of the
objection filed by the petitioner under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation
Act, 1996 in Arbitration Case No. 34 of 2018 (National Highway Authority of India
Vs. M/s Jamini Pharmaceuticals and another).

2. Brief facts of the present case are that an agricultural land falling in Khasra No.
286 measuring 925 sq. m. situated in Mauza - Khanpur, Pargana and Tehsil -
Bhagwanpur, District - Haridwar was acquired by the National Highway Authority
under the National Highway Act, 1956 for widening of national highway no. 73.

A
notification for acquisition of land under Section 3A was published on 27.12.2023 in two widely circulated newspapers and after inviting objections, the acquisition proceedings were completed.
A Notification under Section 3D of the Act was also issued.

Thereafter, the matter came up before the District Judge, Haridwar and Arbitration Case No. 38 of 2018 was registered in which objections were filed under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 on 21.02.2021.

Objection, as filed under Section 34 of the Act, pertains to quantum of compensation as awarded and the basis is that it was not correctly calculated and even rate of the acquired land has not been properly determined.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that though the objection under Section 34 of the Act was filed on 21.02.2021, however, said objection has yet not been M/S Jamini Pharmaceuticals vs National Highway Authority Of India on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95496245/
1 decided and respondent, herein, is adopting delaying tactics.

sentences.text: He further submits that the land has been acquired despite this proper compensation has not been awarded and petitioner is seriously prejudiced, therefore, a direction be issued to the District Judge, Haridwar to decide the objection under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, as expeditiously as possible.
4. The prayer, as sought in the present petition, appears to be innocuous.

Since,
petitioner has already filed objection under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, which is pending for consideration before the District Judge,
Haridwar, therefore, this Court thinks it proper in the interest of justice that a direction be issued to expedite and decide the objection under Section 34 of the Act,
as expeditiously as possible.

5. Accordingly, present petition is disposed of finally with a direction to the learned District Judge, Haridwar to decide the objection preferred by the petitioner under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 bearing Misc. Arbitration Objection No. 27 of 2021 filed in Arbitration Case No. 38 of 2018 (National Highway Authority Vs. M/s Jamini Pharmaceuticals and another) as expeditiously as possible preferably within six months from the date of production of certified copy of this order.
